posts.title: The Piano Man – Not Just a Modern Day Rock Song
posts.content:
The Piano Man – Not Just a Modern Day Rock Song

When Billy Joel released "Piano Man" in 1973, he cemented the piano's place in modern rock history. But the piano's role in popular music stretches back far further than that iconic harmonica intro.

The Piano in Popular Music

From ragtime and jazz to rock and pop, the piano has been at the heart of musical innovation for over a century. Artists like Elton John, Stevie Wonder, and Alicia Keys have all built legendary careers around their piano mastery.

Why Learn Piano?

Learning piano provides a foundation that translates to virtually every other instrument. Understanding chord structures, melody, and harmony becomes intuitive when you can visualize them on the keyboard.

posts.title: Percussion Instruments: Drumming to the Beat of Your Own Music
posts.content:
Percussion Instruments: Drumming to the Beat of Your Own Music

Percussion is the heartbeat of music. From ancient tribal drums to modern electronic drum kits, rhythm has always been the driving force behind every genre.

Types of Percussion Instruments

The percussion family is vast and diverse:

  • Drum Kit — The backbone of rock, pop, jazz, and R&B
  • Congas & Bongos — Essential for Latin and world music
  • Timpani — The powerhouse of the orchestra
  • Snare Drum — Versatile across marching bands and orchestras
  • Cymbals — Adding texture and accents to any ensemble

Benefits of Learning Drums

Drumming improves coordination, timing, and even cognitive function. Studies show that drummers have a unique ability to maintain steady internal timing that benefits all areas of life.

Our drum lessons in West Island cover all styles and levels. Whether you want to rock out or refine your jazz chops, our Pointe-Claire instructors have you covered.

posts.title: History of the Guitar
posts.content:
History of the Guitar

The guitar's origins trace back thousands of years, with stringed instruments appearing in ancient civilizations across the Middle East and Europe. The modern six-string guitar we know today evolved from the Spanish vihuela of the 15th century.

The Evolution of the Guitar

The guitar has undergone remarkable transformations:

  • Classical Guitar — Nylon strings, developed in the 19th century by Antonio Torres
  • Steel-String Acoustic — The American innovation that defined folk and country music
  • Electric Guitar — Revolutionized by Gibson and Fender in the 1950s
  • Bass Guitar — Leo Fender's creation that changed the rhythm section forever

posts.title: The Sounds of Modern Music
posts.content:
The Sounds of Modern Music

Modern music is a melting pot of genres, technologies, and cultural influences. From electronic dance music to neo-soul, today's musical landscape is more diverse than ever before.

How Technology Has Changed Music

Digital audio workstations (DAWs), synthesizers, and recording software have democratized music production. But even in this digital age, the fundamentals of music theory, rhythm, and performance remain essential.

The Importance of Musical Training

Whether you aspire to produce electronic music, join a rock band, or perform classical concertos, a strong musical foundation makes all the difference. Understanding scales, chord progressions, and musical structure gives you the tools to create in any genre.

Programs for Modern Musicians

At West Island Conservatory of Music, we offer programs that bridge traditional training with modern music:

  • Recording Programming — Learn the basics of music production
  • Rock Band — Collaborate with other musicians in a band setting
  • Garage Band — Build confidence through group performance

posts.title: How to Decide Which Guitar to Buy
posts.content:
How to Decide Which Guitar to Buy

Choosing your first (or next) guitar can be overwhelming with so many options available. Here's a practical guide to help you make the right choice.

Acoustic vs. Electric

Acoustic guitars are great for beginners — no amp needed, portable, and they build finger strength. Electric guitars are easier on the fingers and offer more versatility in sound.

Key Factors to Consider

  • Budget — Quality beginner guitars start around $200-400 CAD
  • Size — Younger players may need 3/4 size guitars
  • Genre — Classical music calls for nylon strings; rock demands electric
  • Playability — Always try before you buy
  • Brand — Established brands like Gibson, Fender, and Gretsch offer reliability

Try Before You Buy at Our Store

Our West Island music store at Plaza Pointe-Claire carries Gibson, Fender, and Gretsch guitars. We also offer instrument rentals so you can try an instrument before committing to a purchase.

Our guitar teachers can also help recommend the right instrument for your level and goals.

Visit us at 269 St-Jean blvd, Suite 101, Pointe-Claire, or call 514-428-5080.

The saxophone is one of the most expressive instruments, spanning jazz, blues, rock, and classical music. Our sax instructors teach alto, tenor, and soprano saxophone.

Clarinet Lessons

A staple of orchestral and jazz music, the clarinet develops excellent breath control and musical expression.

Bass Lessons

Learn electric or upright bass and become the rhythmic foundation of any ensemble. Bass players are always in demand!

From jazz to classical, the trumpet is a powerful and versatile brass instrument. Our teachers guide students from first notes to advanced performance.

Violin Lessons
